claims.text: As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has room-temperature tensile ductility of 8–16%.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Pack aluminization will enrich the near-surface region of cast HfNbTaTiZr in aluminum.
A subsequent oxidation step will convert surface aluminum into Al2O3.
The treatment will form a thin, continuous, adherent Al2O3 surface layer.
Al2O3 formed on the alloy surface is thermodynamically stable and slow-growing under the proposed conditions.
The Al2O3 layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
The Al2O3 scale will inhibit oxygen ingress into the bulk HfNbTaTiZr alloy.
Inhibiting oxygen ingress will reduce oxidation-induced degradation at 1000 °C in air.
Aluminized specimens will exhibit lower oxidation mass gain than untreated cast specimens after approximately 100 hours at 1000 °C in air.
Aluminized specimens will develop a thinner oxide scale than untreated cast specimens after approximately 100 hours at 1000 °C in air.
The treatment will leave the underlying alloy microstructure largely unaltered.
The treatment and oxidation exposure will cause little to no reduction in room-temperature tensile ductility relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The treatment and oxidation exposure will cause little to no reduction in high-temperature yield strength relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The alumina coating can remain adherent during approximately 100 hours of high-temperature exposure.

contradictions.description: The boundary describes maintaining both ductility and yield strength under 1000 °C-in-air testing, whereas the predicted outcome and measurements specify room-temperature ductility but 1000 °C yield strength. The intended temperature for the ductility comparison is therefore inconsistent.
